sections.text: And I see adverse omens, O Kesava. I do not see any good in killing my kinsmen in battle.
न काङ्क्षे विजयं कृष्ण न च राज्यं सुखानि च।
I desire not victory, O Krishna, nor kingdom, nor pleasures. Of what avail is dominion to us, O Krishna, or pleasures or even life?
येषामर्थे काङ्क्षितं नो राज्यं भोगाः सुखानि च।
Those for whose sake we desire kingdom, enjoyments and pleasures, stand here in battle, having renounced life and wealth.

We had been discussing Chapter 1, Arjuna Vishada Yoga, the Yoga of Arjunas Grief. We have been seeing various characters involved in this Mahabharata. It reminds me of something I had read in our scriptural literature: Yat Pinde Tat Brahmande, that which is at the microcosm is at the macrocosm.
If I find something in me, Ill be able to find it in the cosmos. The master plan for the microcosm and macrocosm is one and the same. So if I find something in macrocosm, I should also be able to find in microcosm, at my individual level, the efficient cause and material cause for the universe.
The same efficient cause and material cause for me. Therefore, if I can observe something in the universe, I can also apply that to my own life. Something similar is being said for Mahabharata.
As we have discussed before, Mahabharata contains all human situations and characters. So if I find a character in Mahabharata, and if I introspect very carefully, Ill find that character in me too, in my own personality. Let me find Dhritarashtra in me, blinded by attachment to his children, he cannot see what is right and wrong when it comes to them.
I can also probably find Duryodhana in me. Duryodhana wanted to keep something which came accidentally to him, and he doesnt want to give it up. Many internet millionaires in the late 90s and early 2000s went through exactly this.
I actually know one person in particular who made millions in technology, and once he got out of that, he made all his efforts to retain it and failed miserably. Thats Duryodhana in us. Something came to us accidentally, but we dont want to give it up.
We also find Bhishma in us, someone who rigidly follows the rules but ignores the principles. When it comes to paying taxes, we are more like Bhishma. If I can find that I meet the IRS criteria for not paying any taxes, even though I am a multi-billion dollar corporation, thats perfectly legal.
But I completely forget the principle of paying taxes. Its for the social welfare. If I dont pay anything, Im not contributing anything to the social welfare.
So I may find Bhishma in me who is rigidly following the rules but forgetting the principles. I may find Arjuna in me who is very keen on overcoming the obstacles which are in his path of his happiness, what we think is rightfully his. He wants to get over those obstacles.
In this case, Duryodhana. Duryodhana is in his path of finding that happiness, of getting that kingdom back. We have all enthusiasm to march forward towards our success.
And if there is anything in our way, going to get rid of it. But we hope that we also find Krishna in us who says, well, look at it comprehensively. So Krishna said, look at all these people.
All the Kurus are gathered here not only on the other side, but also on your side. The Kurus on your side too. Look at them basically reminding, look at the situation, what youre trying to achieve.
How many people have to make what kind of sacrifices for you to achieve your own goal? In our enthusiasm to achieve success and move forward in our life, we completely forget how many people are making sacrifices for us on our own side. From our family, from your friends, from your relative. Lots of people have to do a lot of things so that I can move forward in my life.
That is one point we forget to acknowledge. We never say thank you to people who supported us, who brought me to this level. But we also, I am a self made man.
I came here with $8 in my pocket. Im not sure that the young generation understands. My generation understands.
India used to have restriction that only you can take $8 in foreign exchange when you leave India. So people very proudly say, I came with $8 and look at what I accomplished. We forget to acknowledge what my parents did to get to the point where I can take the $8 and come here.
So Krishna reminds us that look at on all sides. Make sure that you understand that lots of people have to make lots of sacrifices for you to come to a point where you are capable of overcoming the obstacles which you perceive as the obstacles in the path of happiness. The message we get here is not only that we should introspect negative in us, but also we should introspect and find that Krishnas voice in us.
Then see what is the guidance here. Arjuna now sees the situation in its totality. He looks at how many people are gathered Here and the impact on him is what we are now seeing from Sanjays description.
So Sanjaya says, Krupaya Paraya Vistaha Visidhan Idham Abhravit. Overwhelmed by great compassion or pity, he sorrowfully said this. So Sanjaya says by observing who are gathered on both sides that Arjuna came over with immense pity or compassion.
But hes sorrowful that Im not going to achieve the goal I came here to achieve. I came here to eliminate the evil of Duryodhana, then establish the kingdom which is rightfully ours. So he is now conflicted about whether it is good for him to continue or it will be very noble of him to walk away from the situation.
We see this situation many times. The student is very bright and he wants to go to Harvard. Then he realizes family has to make the sacrifice the family cannot afford.
Come from a poor family. They say it will be okay, Ill go to community college. Out of the compassion for his family members.
So Bhagavan says, well look at is this the situation here? So we hear from Arjuna. I say Dristwa Imam Swajanam K Krishna Yuyutsum Sam Upasthitam by seeing all the dear ones gathered here and eager to fight. Sidanti mama gatrani, my limbs are failing me. I am the mightiest warrior but I dont have any strength. Mukham cha parishushyati, my mouth is drying up, my body is shivering.
Im having goosebumps. Im overwhelmed by fear, very fearful. You get goosebumps when youre either fearful or too excited.
So in verses 28-29 he describes his physical condition. Medical professionals will say this is a nervous breakdown situation. So Arjuna basically had the symptoms of a nervous breakdown.
The next verse says Gandhivam sramsate hastat tvak chaiva paridahyate, na cha shaknomi avasthatum bhramativa cha me manaha, I cant even hold my bow Gandiva, which I rely on, which I have mastered. But right now, given my physical condition, Im not capable. My body is failing me.
The Gandiva is slipping from my hand and my skin is burning. I am also unable to stand. Na cha shaknomi avasthatum, I cant even stand. I need to sit down, I need to lie down. Bhramativa cha me manaha, my mind is whirling.
So he is describing his mental condition as well. Im having this physical sickness. I am losing strength but I am also having an anxiety attack.
So basically he is having a nervous breakdown, an anxiety attack. And what happens when you cannot control that situation? Verse 31 says Nimittani cha pashyami viparitani Keshava, I now see things strangely. On one hand, I cant even think straight, whats going on? I cant even stand.
But now I can see clearly, Nimittani, omens. I can clearly see viparitani Keshava, adverse omens, that something bad is going to happen. This is delusion. When we start having superstitions, oh, because I woke up on this side of the bed, then this will happen, these are things which I know intellectually are not possible.
A black cat crossing my path cannot have any effect on what Im going to do when I get to my office. But my mind says otherwise. That is because Im not listening to my buddhi, my intellect,.
Instead, Im listening to something I heard before, some superstition, and Im believing in it. So now Arjuna is clearly exhibiting the signs of delusion. Nimittani cha pashyami viparitani Keshava, na cha shreyo anupashyami hatva svajanam ahave, I do not see any good coming out of killing my own people in battle. So he has gone from I cant comprehend this situation which Im facing, therefore Im losing the strength.
Im having this physical symptoms of nervous breakdown. Im having anxiety attack. How Im going to handle this thing.
Now I come to the conclusion that this is probably not the right thing to do. So now Im creating my own reality and then believing it. More I stay in that condition, more I believe in it.
The intellect which is normally guiding you is not available to you, but you create an alternate reality. And now I have all the good reason to believe in the realities. So Im now believing in that alternate universe which Im living in.
And then I have all the justification. So the justification, my mind is creating the justifications, not intellect. So intellect has basically resigned from guiding you.
Mind takes over and says I have all the answers. Let me tell you what is happening here in that state of that anxiety and delusion. A dream like situation.
In dream we create our own reality. That reality at that time is very real to me. Somebody whos dreaming, you try to convince him youre dreaming.
Obviously he will not listen to you as long as hes in dream. Only if he wakes up from that dream, he will listen to you this delusion is something similar to that. That reality is so real for that person that he is not willing to accept the other reality which other people see as the real.
Therefore, when you have any kind of a mental disorder, you go to some professional psychiatrist. Because if you talk to your relatives or friends, you will not listen to them say, no, no, I know, but maybe you listen to somebody who you think is third party, who has no X to grind in your life, and you tell him. Then in the end he says, okay, thats fine, our session is over.
The charges are $350 an hour. He said, you suddenly come out of your depression. How many hours can I spend here? But thats obviously because you are someone who is not invested in your situation.
And youre seeing from his perspective. And that person tells you Krishna obviously is that person. Krishna is the psychiatrist here.
The good news is Arjuna has faith in Krishna. First his argument going forward why he should not be in this situation. Now, how this situation came upon him is obviously up to our imagination, but we have seen the description of whats happening.
If this is an effect, that this is what happened to Arjuna, there is a cause for it. So the cause can be only one of the two causes. Sanjaya said he was overwhelmed by the pity and compassion that I can be the cause for destruction of all my relatives.
So that may be one cause. Maybe he felt that compassion that how can I be the cause for my people and all the people on the other side to be killed? There is another reason this can happen. He realized the task at hand is not as simple as he thought, because he never imagined a situation other than him winning.
All I have to do is get rid of Duryodhana, win this war and the kingdom will be rightfully mine. He never thought about what support Duryodhana will have. Duryodhana support from Bheeshma, Drona, Kurupacharya, all those great warriors who are as good or better than him.

In verse 31, Arjuna says: Nimittani cha pashyami viparitani, I see adverse omens, portents of disaster. This is the mark of a mind slipping into delusion. When were overwhelmed, we begin to see signs and superstitions where there is only cause and effect. The black cat crossing our path cannot affect our business meeting, yet in states of anxiety, the rational mind abdicates and magical thinking takes over. Notice Arjunas reasoning in verses 32-33: I desire not victory, nor kingdom, nor pleasures. Those for whose sake we desire these things, they stand here ready to sacrifice their lives and wealth. This sounds noble, even wise. But a critical insight: when the intellect (buddhi) abandons its guiding role, the mind creates an alternate reality that feels completely valid. Arjuna has constructed a seemingly logical argument, but its built on the foundation of emotional overwhelm, not clear seeing. Reflect on times when youve created elaborate justifications for avoidance. Im not taking that opportunity because it would mean sacrificing family time, when really, fear of failure was driving the decision. Im staying in this situation out of loyalty, when actually, fear of change kept you stuck. The Gita teaches us to examine not just the content of our reasoning but its source. Is your decision emerging from clear-headed assessment or from emotional chaos that has dressed itself in logical clothing? This week, when you find yourself constructing arguments against action, pause and ask: Is my buddhi guiding me, or has my mind hijacked the process and started manufacturing convenient truths?
